contexts.text: When a man is in a state of heavenly love or affection, he is then in an angelic state, namely, as it were not in time, if there is no impatience in that affection; for impatience is a corporeal affection; and in proportion as a man is in it, he is in time; but in proportion as he is not at the same time in it, he is not in time.
(The lower sort of those who belong to the province of the infundibulum) are... prone to suspicion, impatient... SE 915.
They thus add impatience, which creates the greatest pain, and induces such a weakness of body that [the man] can scarcely raise himself from his bed.
